title: §26-002: Reverse Proxies, Load Balancers & Zero-Downtime Deployments
description: Multiple-choice practice questions and deep runtime verification for §26-002 (Reverse Proxies, Load Balancers & Zero-Downtime Deployments).

cards.concept: Reverse Proxies, Load Balancers & Zero-Downtime Deployments: Reverse Proxy Architecture & TLS Termination
cards.question: Why should production Node.js microservices be deployed behind a reverse proxy (e.g. NGINX, HAProxy, Envoy) rather than exposed directly to the public internet?

options.text: Node.js cannot listen on port 443.
The reverse proxy offloads TLS termination, buffers slow clients (Slowloris defense), serves static assets, provides load balancing, and rate limits traffic before reaching Node.js.
Reverse proxies rewrite JavaScript code into machine code.
Direct Node.js ports are blocked by modern browsers.

cards.explanation: Reverse proxies excel at handling thousands of idle connections, terminating SSL handshakes, and buffering requests. This frees the Node.js event loop to focus entirely on application logic.
cards.pitfall: Failing to configure `app.set('trust proxy', true)` causes Express to misidentify proxy IP addresses as the client IP, breaking rate limiters.
cards.citation: NGINX Documentation: Reverse Proxy Architecture / Node.js Production Guide

cards.concept: Reverse Proxies, Load Balancers & Zero-Downtime Deployments: Circuit Breaker Pattern in Microservices
cards.question: What are the three states of a Circuit Breaker (e.g. Opossum), and how does it prevent cascaded system failure?

options.text: Read, Write, Execute.
Closed (normal traffic), Open (failing downstream; fast-fail immediately without calling remote service), and Half-Open (trial traffic to test downstream recovery).
TCP, UDP, ICMP.
Active, Inactive, Suspended.

cards.explanation: When failures exceed a threshold, the breaker trips Open, fast-failing traffic instantly. After a cooldown, it enters Half-Open to test recovery, preventing thread and socket exhaustion.
cards.pitfall: Not setting fallback handlers on circuit breakers causes uncaught exceptions during downstream outages.
cards.citation: Release It! (Michael Nygard) / Opossum Circuit Breaker Guide
